subtopic: Learning a craft by deliberate practice
passage: Note for Aditi's parents, from her violin teacher. Aditi arrived early and played the opening piece from last term, the one she has known by heart since March. She played it three times, smiling each time, and asked if she could play it again. When I turned to the new page with the fast finger shifts, she said her hand was tired. So I asked her to play only the four hard bars, slowly, five times, and we marked each try with a pencil tick. By the fifth try the notes were cleaner. She frowned but stayed. Please let her start home practice with those four bars. Damini, music teacher

qa.q: How many times did Aditi play the old piece when she arrived?
qa.a: She played it three times, smiling each time.

qa.q: What might Aditi be feeling when she says her hand is tired at the new page?
qa.a: She is probably uneasy or discouraged. The old piece feels good and the new page is hard, so a tired hand may be a way to avoid the difficult part.

qa.q: What small step could Aditi's parents take to help at home?
qa.a: They could ask her to play the four hard bars slowly at the start of practice, before the piece she already knows.

qa.q: How does Damini see Aditi's repeated playing of the old piece?
qa.a: Damini sees it as enjoyable but not much practice, which is why the teacher moved her to the hard bars and marked each try.

grounding: Shows a child repeating a mastered violin piece because it feels good while the difficult bars are where growth lives.

subtopic: Learning a craft by deliberate practice
passage: Tuesday evening. Played my favourite keyboard tune again, the rain song. Six times! It feels so nice when my fingers already know where to go. Deepika didi came in and listened and said it sounded lovely, then asked why I never play the second page. I said it's boring and I get it wrong. She said the wrong bit is where fingers learn. She showed me just two bars, left hand only, very slowly. I got them wrong seven times and I was cross. Then once right. Tomorrow I will do the two bars before the rain song, not after. Leela

qa.q: How many times did Leela play the rain song?
qa.a: Leela played the rain song six times.

qa.q: Why was Leela cross while practising the two bars?
qa.a: Leela felt frustrated because getting the two bars wrong seven times felt worse than the easy tune that always goes right. 😕

qa.q: What choice did Leela make for the next day's practice?
qa.a: Leela decided to play the two bars before the rain song instead of after, so the hard part comes first.

qa.q: How does Deepika see the wrong notes Leela plays?
qa.a: Deepika treats the wrong notes as the place where fingers learn, so the second page is worth the effort.

grounding: Shows a child replaying an already easy tune for pleasure and only later working on the hard bars.
